chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Nuhayki, from Ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from a number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Qasri, who said:

I was in charge of al-Madinah, and a غلام who had stolen was brought to me. So I asked Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about him, and he said: “Ask him whether, at the time he stole, he knew that there was a punishment upon him for theft. If he says yes, then say to him: What is that punishment? If he did not know that for theft there is amputation upon him, then let him go.”
He said: So I took the غلام and questioned him, and I said to him: Did you know that there is a punishment for theft? He said: Yes. I said: What is it? He said: Beating. So I let him go.

key_terms.السَّرِقَةِ: the act of theft as the legal offense under discussion
key_terms.الضَّرْبُ: beating, the punishment the غلام thought applied to theft
key_terms.عُقُوبَةً: a punishment or penal consequence for the offense
key_terms.فَخَلِّ عَنْهُ: release him and do not proceed with the hadd punishment
key_terms.قَطْعًا: amputation, the prescribed hadd punishment referred to here

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd punishment for theft applied if the thief did not know the prescribed penalty?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns the legal ruling of theft and shows that the fixed punishment is not applied when the offender did not know the specific prescribed penalty. Imam Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام instructs that the accused be questioned regarding his knowledge, and when he proves ignorant of the punishment of amputation, he is released.
